```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = FALSE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(AKsf)
library(ggplot2)
```

AKsf uses the same building-block approach as nzsf: getters return `sf` objects,
and plotters add `geom_sf` layers. The bundled snapshots make this tutorial work
offline. Source definitions and derivations are documented in the repository’s
`DATA_SOURCES.md`.

```{r map}
ggplot() +
  plot_reporting_areas(c("541", "542", "543"), fill = "#b5d9e8",
                        colour = "#345b6c", linewidth = 0.3) +
  plot_coast(fill = "grey88", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.15) +
  coord_aksf() + theme_aksf()
```

`coord_aksf()` and the default projected getters keep the western Aleutians near
the rest of Alaska. A geographic longitude range can instead span nearly the
entire world. Use the same CRS for data and analytical operations.

## Plans and agency units

```{r plans}
get_fmp_catalog()[, c("fmp_id", "plan_name")]
fmp <- get_fmp_areas(c("BSAI_GF", "GOA_GF"))
fmp[, c("fmp_id", "geometry_basis", "boundary_status")]
```

The six FMPs overlap across fisheries. Salmon has East, West, and Cook Inlet
features. Crab extends eastward to Scotch Cap south of the Aleutians, whereas
the BSAI groundfish boundary is farther west. These broad reference polygons do
not describe stock boundaries, closures, or permission to fish.

## Joining reporting areas to observations

```{r join}
observations <- data.frame(station = c("west", "central"),
                           longitude = c(-176, -172), latitude = c(52, 53))
points <- sf::st_as_sf(observations, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)
points <- sf::st_transform(points, proj_aksf())
areas <- get_reporting_areas(c("541", "542", "543"))
# Dissolve multipart source records by code before assigning a code to points.
by_code <- aggregate(areas["area_code"], by = list(code = areas$area_code), FUN = unique)
hits <- sf::st_intersects(points, by_code)
# Zero matches are outside coverage; multiple matches may lie on a boundary.
points$n_matches <- lengths(hits)
points$reporting_area <- vapply(hits, function(i) {
  if (length(i) == 1L) by_code$code[i] else NA_character_
}, character(1))
sf::st_drop_geometry(points)
```

Do not silently choose the first polygon for a boundary point. State-water areas
and the Donut Hole are not interchangeable with U.S. federal FMP coverage.

## ADF&G codes and provenance

```{r adfg}
registration <- get_registration_areas()
sf::st_drop_geometry(registration)[, c("area_code", "area_name")]
# The complete six-digit groundfish statistical layer is also bundled:
# stat <- get_statistical_areas()
# federal <- stat[stat$WATERS_CODE == "FED", ]
```

Use character strings for joins with area codes. ADF&G’s native hierarchy and
source date fields remain available. Groundfish polygons are not universal
reporting grids for every fishery.

```{r provenance}
# A JSON manifest, readable without installing additional runtime packages.
cat(head(get_sources(), 10), sep = "\n")
```

Retrieval dates identify the snapshot, not when a boundary became legally
effective. In particular, NOAA ATB’s salmon West source has a 2023 edit date;
AKsf separates Cook Inlet following the 2024 plan but does not certify every
source exclusion against later amendments. For regulatory work consult current
NOAA, ADF&G, and NPFMC materials.
